correctness.rationale: Every proper ideal has a full-support leading code because its projection onto each nonzero uniserial branch has a smallest degree, and multiplication by that branch generator forces all subsequent pure powers into the ideal. Multiplying arbitrary lifts changes leading coefficients by coordinatewise products and adds the leading degrees, with zero contributions beyond truncation. Full support and absence of zero divisors guarantee no surviving coordinate can disappear. The inverse-image construction completes both containments and iteration yields exact nilpotency indices. Independent exhaustive direct multiplication and code-prediction calculations agree for 14,062 ordered pairs across five small fields/algebras.

originality.rationale: The prior own all-ideal dimension-spectrum result for exactly this ring already supplies the ideal parametrization, so no independent novelty is assigned to that parametrization or to counting ideals. Its claim does not give the ideal-product rule, Hadamard correspondence, or nilpotency-index formula. Behboodi–Shojaee (arXiv:1201.6076) gives general cyclic-decomposition properties and a concrete two-branch ring example, not multiplication of all ideals. Randriambololona (arXiv:1312.0022) develops Schur multiplication on abstract linear codes, not its realization as a truncated-branch ideal monoid. value.rationale: The multiplication monoid of all ideals is a natural ring invariant stronger than the ideal count and dimension distribution. The exact law explains how mixed nonmonomial ideals multiply, when Schur products preserve coupling versus create pure branches, and gives explicit zero-product and nilpotency-index criteria uniformly for arbitrary branch counts, truncation lengths, and fields. This is a complete structural determination of a natural algebraic operation, not a routine numerical increment.
